title: Edit the recorded Scan Store architecture line to sort-on-read, and close the sort-on-read question on the measured numbers
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: The engine's recorded Scan Store architecture line reads sort-on-read (children ordered largest first on read, no stored order) instead of 'stored sorted largest first': unknown
The sort-on-read question is closed, i.e. recorded as decided on the measured numbers: partial

How does the engine's Scan Store architecture line actually get edited? The build check found no write path from this worktree, and SL-042's build hit the same wall, which is why this slice exists. If the build stage has no path, someone with access to the engine record must apply the clause, or the slice can only pass with criterion 1 unmet and unknown. Should validate accept that, or must the edit be seen in the record itself?

A new docs/design/SL-068-sort-on-read.md plus a pointer, versus appending a 'Closed' section to the SL-042 doc in place. The design follows the one-doc-per-slice convention. The single-file alternative touches one fewer file.
Pointer line appended to the SL-042 doc, versus editing lines 120-126 in place. Appending keeps the history, and in-place editing leaves no stale 'still open' wording.
No fitness rule or new test guards 'no stored order' in Core. Someone may want a rule anyway, even though it would rest on a guessed code shape.
Carrying the old and new wording verbatim in the decision doc, versus only the new sentence. The doc labels it submitted text and not a copy of the record.
